summary: We developed ARES-NAV, an AI-powered Martian Extravehicular Activity (EVA) surface exploration and pathfinding copilot built for the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge.   On Mars, communication delays with Earth reach up to 24 minutes one-way, preventing real-time Mission Control guidance while astronauts navigate steep scarps, wheel-trapping loose sand, radiation spikes, and radio dead zones. Existing planetary viewers display orbital datasets in isolation, leaving crews without unified survival intelligence.   ARES-NAV solves this by fusing five NASA datasets—MOLA, HiRISE, THEMIS, CRISM, and RAD—into an interactive Three.js / WebGL 3D terrain engine calibrated for Jezero Crater and Mount Sharp. A lightweight MobileNetV3 neural network runs natively in the browser via ONNX WebAssembly with zero cloud latency to classify surface hazards in real time. These predictions feed into a multi-objective A^* pathfinder that generates Safest, Fastest, Science-Max, and Emergency Abort routes while tracking dual-crew biometrics, oxygen reserves, and dynamic Point-of-No-Return limits.   By turning fragmented orbital data into autonomous, offline-capable survival decisions, ARES-NAV empowers analog crews and future human explorers to navigate Mars safely.
details:
ARES-NAV is an AI-powered Martian EVA exploration and survival copilot. Because Earth–Mars communication delays reach 24 minutes one-way, crews cannot rely on live Mission Control. ARES-NAV fuses five NASA datasets (MOLA, HiRISE, THEMIS, CRISM, and RAD) into an interactive Three.js/WebGL 3D terrain engine for Jezero Crater and Mount Sharp. A MobileNetV3 neural network runs locally in the browser via ONNX WebAssembly with zero server latency to classify sand traps, scarps, bedrock, and regolith. These predictions feed into a multi-objective A^* pathfinder that generates Safest, Fastest, Science-Max, and Emergency Abort shelter routes while tracking dual-crew biometrics, suit oxygen burn, and a dynamic Point-of-No-Return boundary.
ARES-NAV replaces fragmented planetary viewers with unified, offline-capable survival intelligence. Ready today as a zero-install web app for Mars analog habitats (MDRS, HI-SEAS) and researchers, its edge-AI architecture scales directly to future human Mars missions and astronaut AR helmet HUDs.

  • Tech Stack: React, Vite, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, WebGL, Python, PyTorch, ONNX, and onnxruntime-web (WebAssembly).
  • NASA Data: MOLA, HiRISE, THEMIS, CRISM, RAD, and PDS rover/visor telemetry (Mastcam-Z, Navcam, SuperCam).

    Unlike rover planners focused only on wheel slip, ARES-NAV prioritizes human EVA physiology—coupling slope (>15 degrees), thermal inertia, UHF line-of-sight comms shadows, and solar storm radiation directly with metabolic workload, carried sample mass, and oxygen Point-of-No-Return limits.
